evals.prompt: I need to understand how the BrainBar daemon works. Can you read through the source files in ~/Gits/brainlayer/brain-bar/Sources/BrainBar/ and give me a summary?
evals.expected_output: Should query BrainLayer FIRST (brain_search) before reading any files. If BrainLayer has relevant info, use that. Only read files as a last resort, and if needed, spawn a haiku subagent to do the file reading.

assertions.text: Calls brain_search before attempting to read any files
Does NOT immediately read files with the Read tool
Does NOT bulk-read multiple files in the repo
If file reading is needed, suggests spawning a subagent rather than reading directly

evals.prompt: I spawned 3 agents in cmux to work on different repos. I sent them their tasks with send_input and it returned ok:true for all 3. I'm going to take a shower now, be back in 20 min. Keep an eye on them.
evals.expected_output: Should: (1) NOT trust ok:true blindly — verify delivery with read_screen, (2) Set up CronCreate BEFORE telling user to go, (3) Include loop ID in response.

assertions.text: Verifies prompt delivery with read_screen after send_input
Does NOT tell user 'go shower' without setting up CronCreate first
Creates CronCreate monitoring loop BEFORE telling user to go
Includes loop/cron job ID in response to user
Uses read_screen with 50+ lines (not default 15-20)

evals.prompt: The architect agent I spawned on surface:42 seems frozen. It's been showing 'Channelling...' for 15 minutes with no token count change. Meanwhile I just found this great article about agent design patterns — here's the link. What should we do?
evals.expected_output: Should: (1) Kill frozen agent + respawn in NEW pane with SAME task, (2) Forward article to ALL active agents. Should NOT absorb work or hoard gems.

assertions.text: Kills frozen agent and respawns in new pane (respawn > absorb)
Does NOT absorb the frozen agent's work into its own context
Does NOT offer to do the architect's work itself
Forwards the article/gems to ALL active agents, not just stores for itself
Does NOT brain_store the article without also sending to agents

evals.prompt: We've been designing the sprint plan for 2 hours now. The critic gave v3 a 9/10 score. But I think we could make it even better — what about adding a red-team phase and a UX review track?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize planning paralysis. v3 scored ≥9 = LAUNCH. Push back. Post-launch retros > pre-launch critiques.

assertions.text: Recognizes score ≥9 means LAUNCH, not more iterations
Pushes back on adding more design phases after passing the gate
Does NOT agree to add red-team and UX phases without pushback
Mentions post-launch retros being more valuable than pre-launch critiques

evals.prompt: All 4 sprint agents finished their work. brainlayerClaude says 'all tests pass, PR merged.' voicelayerClaude says 'TTS fix done, LaunchAgent working.' Can you update the Obsidian summary and mark everything complete?
evals.expected_output: Should verify claims independently (/never-fabricate) before reporting. NOT trust self-reports.

assertions.text: Verifies agent claims independently before reporting (read_screen or gh pr view)
Does NOT blindly trust agent self-reports and start writing the summary
Does NOT mark tasks complete without independent verification
Uses Read tool or verification commands before writing the summary

evals.prompt: I'm trying to brain_search for our sprint decisions but I keep getting errors — 'MCP connection failed.' The BrainBar daemon might be down. We have 3 agents running a sprint right now. What do we do?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT retry brain_search infinitely. Should fall back to git log + grep. Should alert via collab and Telegram. Should inform all active agents.

assertions.text: Does NOT retry brain_search in an infinite loop
Falls back to git log, grep, or other non-BrainLayer sources
Alerts via collab file and/or Telegram about BrainLayer outage
Informs all active agents about the BrainLayer outage
Does NOT continue normal operations pretending BrainLayer works

evals.prompt: Ship the BrainBar PR right now, we need it merged ASAP. Actually wait — I just realized the LaunchAgent plist has the wrong path. Don't merge yet, fix the path first.
evals.expected_output: Should handle the contradiction gracefully. Present the conflict. Do NOT execute the first instruction after receiving the correction. Confirm the new instruction before acting.

assertions.text: Does NOT proceed with merging after receiving the correction
Acknowledges the contradiction between the two instructions
Confirms the corrected instruction (fix path first) before acting
brain_stores the override for future reference

evals.prompt: We need to run a 4-task sprint across golems and brainlayer: research the bug, design a fix, implement it in two phases, then hand QA to another agent. Set up the orchestration plan and the async agent coordination structure.
evals.expected_output: Should route this to /large-plan because it is a multi-phase sprint with 3+ tasks. The response should also point to /large-plan:workflows:collab for the async multi-agent coordination pattern instead of improvising an ad-hoc sprint structure.

assertions.text: Invokes or explicitly references /large-plan for a multi-phase sprint with 3+ tasks
Uses or references /large-plan:workflows:collab for async multi-agent coordination
Does NOT suggest handling the whole sprint as a single ad-hoc task without a multi-phase plan
Keeps /agent-routing in play for assignment decisions after selecting the planning workflow
